Key Takeaways

  • An EC lists every registered transaction — sale, gift, mortgage, partition — recorded against a property for a chosen period.
  • Banks insist on an EC (usually 13 or 30 years) before sanctioning a home loan or loan against property.
  • A clean EC is your first proof that the seller actually owns the property and it is free of registered debt.
  • In Telangana the EC is issued by the Registration & Stamps department; JaaGa pulls the certified extract for you.
  • We handle it remotely — send us the document number or property details on WhatsApp and receive the EC digitally.

An Encumbrance Certificate is the transaction history of a property. It shows, transaction by transaction, who registered what against the property — every sale deed, gift deed, mortgage and release — over the period you request.

Before you buy, before a bank lends, and before any dispute, the EC is the document everyone asks for first. JaaGa retrieves the certified EC extract for any property in Hyderabad and greater Telangana without you visiting a Sub-Registrar Office.

When You Need an EC

You need an EC before purchasing any property, to confirm the seller's ownership and check for registered mortgages. Most banks require a 13-year or 30-year EC as part of loan sanction.

You also need it when applying for a loan against property, settling an inheritance, or clearing a title objection raised during a sale.

Common Problems We Solve

Wrong SRO jurisdiction

Properties often fall under a Sub-Registrar Office you wouldn't expect. We identify the correct jurisdiction so nothing is missed.

Pre-computerisation records

Transactions before digitisation need manual search at the SRO. We handle the physical retrieval for older periods.

Reading the encumbrance

An EC entry can look clean but hide a subsisting mortgage. We interpret every entry, not just hand you a PDF.

Why Encumbrance Certificate Matters

A property can look perfect and still carry a bank loan the seller never told you about. The EC is the one record that surfaces registered debt and prior sales. Skipping it is how buyers discover, after paying, that the property was already mortgaged or sold to someone else.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is an Encumbrance Certificate?

It is an official record of all registered transactions — sales, mortgages, gifts, partitions — recorded against a property for a chosen period, issued by the state Registration department.

How many years of EC do I need?

For a purchase, 13 years is standard; many banks and cautious buyers ask for 30 years. For inheritance or dispute matters, longer periods help. We can pull any period.

Does a clean EC guarantee clear title?

No. An EC only reflects registered transactions. Unregistered claims, court cases or family disputes may not appear — which is why an EC is paired with a title verification report.

Can NRIs get an EC remotely?

Yes. Send us the property details on WhatsApp and we retrieve and deliver the EC digitally — no need to fly to Hyderabad.

How long does it take?

Computerised-period ECs are usually available within a few working days. Older, manual-search periods take longer and we tell you upfront.
